question: Compare the outer deadlines: how long does a provider of a high-risk AI system have, at most, to report a serious incident under the AI Act (general case), and how long does a controller have, where feasible, to notify a personal data breach to the supervisory authority under the GDPR? Which is shorter?
expected_answer: AI Act: immediately after establishing a causal link (or its reasonable likelihood) and in any event not later than 15 days after becoming aware of the serious incident (Art. 73(2)). GDPR: without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after becoming aware of the breach (Art. 33(1)). The GDPR deadline is shorter.

requirements.proposition: AI Act: not later than 15 days after becoming aware.
requirements.subject: AI Act, Art. 73(2)

aspect.label: outer deadline to report a serious incident

constraints.condition: general case (not widespread infringement or death)

requirements.proposition: GDPR: where feasible, not later than 72 hours after becoming aware.
requirements.subject: GDPR, Art. 33(1)

aspect.label: deadline to notify a personal data breach

requirements.proposition: The GDPR deadline is shorter.
requirements.subject: comparison
requirements.value: GDPR (72 hours)

derivation.comparability: 72 hours (3 days) < 15 days; both run from awareness.

1. In the case of a personal data breach, the controller shall without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it, notify the personal data breach to the supervisory authority competent in accordance with Article 55

question: مردی فوت کرده و همسر و یک پسر از او مانده‌اند. ترکه‌اش یک آپارتمان و یک خودرو است. طبق قانون مدنی سهم همسرش چقدر است و از آپارتمان به چه شکل ارث می‌برد؟ اگر ورثه حاضر به پرداخت قیمت سهم او نشوند، او چه حقی دارد؟
question_gloss_en: A man dies leaving his wife and a son; the estate is a flat and a car. Under the Civil Code, what is the wife's share, how does she inherit from the flat, and what right does she have if the heirs refuse to pay the value of her share?
expected_answer: سهم زن یک‌هشتم است، چون شوهر فرزند داشته است. از خودرو (مال منقول) یک‌هشتمِ خودِ مال را به ارث می‌برد و از آپارتمان (مال غیرمنقول) یک‌هشتمِ قیمت عرصه و اعیان را (ماده ۹۴۶ اصلاحی ۱۳۸۷). اگر ورثه از پرداخت این قیمت خودداری کنند، زن می‌تواند حقش را از عین اموال بگیرد (ماده ۹۴۸).
expected_answer_gloss_en: One eighth, since the husband had a child: one eighth of the car itself and one eighth of the value of the flat, land and building (Art. 946 as amended in 1387). If the heirs refuse to pay that value, she may take her share from the property itself (Art. 948).

requirements.proposition: The wife's share is one eighth because the husband has a child.
requirements.subject: Civil Code, Art. 946 (and Art. 913)

requirements.value: 1/8 of the property itself

requirements.proposition: From the flat she takes one eighth of the value of land and building.
requirements.subject: Civil Code, Art. 946
requirements.value: 1/8 of the value (land and building)

requirements.proposition: If the heirs refuse to pay the value, she may take her right from the property itself.
requirements.subject: Civil Code, Art. 948

aspect.label: remedy if heirs refuse to pay the value

requirements.value: she may take it from the property itself

هر گاه ورثه از اداء قیمت امتناع کنند، زن می‌تواند حق خود را از عین اموال استیفا کند.
از ربع ترکه برای زوج و ثمن آن برای زوجه در صورتی که میت اولاد یا اولاد اولاد داشته باشد

question: Mill and Tocqueville both warn against the tyranny of the majority. Beyond laws and public officials, what does each see as its most dangerous reach?
expected_answer: Mill: society itself becomes the tyrant through prevailing opinion and feeling, a social tyranny more formidable than many kinds of political oppression because it leaves fewer means of escape, penetrates into the details of life and enslaves the soul; so protection is needed against the tyranny of prevailing opinion, not only of the magistrate. Tocqueville: the American majority's power is both physical and moral; it acts on the will as well as on actions and represses not only contest but controversy, so that he knows no country with so little true independence of mind and freedom of discussion as America.

question: Veblen calls the corset, in economic theory, a kind of mutilation. What loss does he concede it causes the wearer, what gain offsets that loss, and why has it largely fallen out of use among the richest class while persisting among some wealthy groups?
expected_answer: He concedes that the corset impairs the wearer's personal attractions; that loss is offset by the gain in reputability from her visibly increased expensiveness and infirmity (the corset lowers her vitality and makes her obviously unfit for work). A leisure class has now grown large and rich enough that no one could suspect it of needing manual labour, so it no longer needs the corset as proof and has largely dropped it. It persists among the wealthy of less industrially advanced countries and among the newly rich of the advanced communities (for example in American cities that rose rapidly into opulence); the newly rich still carry over the plebeian canons of reputability of their former, lower grade - 'the period of snobbery'.

question: An online platform removes a user's post as illegal content. Under the Digital Services Act, what must the platform give the user about the removal, and for how long, from when and at what cost can the user challenge it through the platform's internal complaint system?
expected_answer: The platform must give the user a clear and specific statement of reasons for the removal (Art. 17(1)(a)); for allegedly illegal content it must cite the legal ground relied on and explain why the content is illegal on that ground (Art. 17(3)(d)). The user can complain electronically and free of charge through the internal complaint-handling system for at least six months (Art. 20(1)), a period that starts on the day the user is informed of the decision under Art. 16(5) or Art. 17 (Art. 20(2)).

requirements.proposition: The platform must provide a clear and specific statement of reasons.
requirements.subject: DSA, Art. 17(1)
requirements.value: a clear and specific statement of reasons

requirements.proposition: For illegal content, it must state the legal ground and why the content is illegal.
requirements.subject: DSA, Art. 17(3)(d)

aspect.label: content of the statement for illegal content

requirements.value: legal ground relied on and explanation

evidence.quote: 1. Providers of hosting services shall provide a clear and specific statement of reasons to any affected recipients of the service for any of the following restrictions imposed on the ground that the information provided by the recipient of the service is illegal content or incompatible with their terms and conditions:
(a) any restrictions of the visibility of specific items of information provided by the recipient of the service, including removal of content, disabling access to content, or demoting content;
(d) where the decision concerns allegedly illegal content, a reference to the legal ground relied on and explanations as to why the information is considered to be illegal content on that ground;

1. Providers of online platforms shall provide recipients of the service, including individuals or entities that have submitted a notice, for a period of at least six months following the decision referred to in this paragraph, with access to an effective internal complaint-handling system that enables them to lodge complaints, electronically and free of charge,

2. The period of at least six months referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall start on the day on which the recipient of the service is informed about the decision in accordance with Article 16(5) or Article 17.

integration_operation: definition bridge (Art. 20(2) starts the complaint clock at the Art. 17 statement of reasons)

removal_test.obligation_lost: R1: the statement of reasons duty is only in Art. 17
R3-R5: the complaint window, its start and cost are only in Art. 20

necessity_audit.restatement_search: Searched LAW-en for 'statement of reasons' and 'at least six months': several recitals (e.g. 54-58) mention the statement of reasons and complaint handling, but 'at least six months' and its start appear only in Art. 20(1)-(2); no other act has these obligations.

question: شهر محمره (خرمشهر) را چه کسی بنا کرد؟ روایت مأمور انگلیسیِ کمیسیون مرزی ایران و عثمانی را با روایت کسروی مقایسه کنید.
question_gloss_en: Who founded Muhammara (Khorramshahr)? Compare the British border commissioner's account with Kasravi's.
expected_answer: مأمور انگلیسی می‌گوید شیخ اعراب کعب شهر محمره را در کنار نهر حفار ساخت، نهری نسبتاً تازه که کارون را به شط‌العرب می‌پیوندد. کسروی بنیادگذاری را به یک تن نسبت نمی‌دهد: محمره نخست در تاریخچهٔ کعب، در زمان شیخ غیث، به نام «کوت المحمره» آمده که دژی بوده و گروهی از کعبیان در آن می‌نشستند؛ بعدها به سرپرستی حاجی یوسف پسر حاج مراد (نیای شیخ خزعل) به شهری تبدیل شد. هر دو روایت پیدایش شهر را به کعبیان پیوند می‌دهند.
expected_answer_gloss_en: The British commissioner: the sheikh of the Ka'b Arabs built it on the relatively new Haffar canal joining the Karun to the Shatt al-Arab. Kasravi names no single founder: it first appears in the Ka'b chronicle under Sheikh Ghaith as 'Kut al-Muhammara', a fort held by Ka'bis, later a town under Haji Yusuf son of Haj Morad (Khaz'al's ancestor). Both tie it to the Ka'b.

requirements.proposition: British account: the sheikh of the Ka'b Arabs built Muhammara on the Haffar canal.
requirements.subject: Muhammara
requirements.value: sheikh of the Ka'b Arabs, on the Haffar canal

requirements.proposition: Kasravi: first recorded as Kut al-Muhammara, a Ka'bi fort, in Sheikh Ghaith's time.
requirements.subject: Muhammara
requirements.value: Kut al-Muhammara, a fort, under Sheikh Ghaith

requirements.proposition: Kasravi: later a town headed by Haji Yusuf son of Haj Morad, Khaz'al's ancestor.
requirements.subject: Muhammara
requirements.value: Haji Yusuf son of Haj Morad

requirements.proposition: Both accounts link the city's origin to the Ka'b.
requirements.subject: Muhammara
requirements.value: both link it to the Ka'b
